correctness.rationale: The planar polygon mixed-area identity is applied with explicit edge lengths and supporting directions. The angular kernel is even and has period 2π/lcm(n,m), with its possible support-index changes on exactly one equally spaced kink grid. On each open grid interval it is a single sinusoid, and reflection about interval midpoints forces a pure positive cosine. The angular mean fixes its exact amplitude; shifting the second argument by π handles excluded area. Modular parity of the phase gives the two-adic criterion. Endpoint angles are included by continuity; all n,m≥3 and R,S>0 are proved. An independent vertex-sum convex-hull implementation passed 1008 numerical checks, which supplement but do not establish the universal proof.

value.rationale: The mixed excluded area is the natural pairwise geometrical kernel used in recent random sequential adsorption comparisons. The result solves its orientation optimization for all side counts and radii with an exact closed formula, reveals an unexpected common-vertex two-adic min/max dichotomy, and produces a scale-free oscillation depending only on lcm(n,m), including the sharp L^{-2} decay. This advances beyond finitely tabulated fixed-angle values and can serve as an analytic input to polygon-mixture models; no direct physical-jamming consequence is claimed.
